title: Universal torsion etale cohomological descent for proper hypercovers
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $a:U_\bullet\to X$ an augmented simplicial scheme: $U_\bullet$ is a functor from the opposite simplex category to schemes, with a natural map to the constant diagram $X$. Write $M_0=X$ and $M_n$ for the finite limit over $X$ of the compatible proper faces of an $n$-simplex ($M_1=U_0\times_XU_0$). Suppose every matching map $U_n\to M_n$ is proper surjective [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Then every augmentation $a_n:U_n\to X$ is proper, and after any $Y\to X$ the base-changed augmented simplicial scheme again has proper surjective matching maps. Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring annihilated by an integer $m\ge1$. On the small etale topoi [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], regard $a$ as the morphism from the total simplicial topos (a sheaf is a family $F_n$ on $U_{n,\mathrm{Et}}$ with compatible maps $u_\alpha^{-1}F_p\to F_q$ for every simplicial structure map $u_\alpha:U_q\to U_p$). For every bounded-below complex $L$ of sheaves of constant $\Lambda$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the adjunction unit is an isomorphism
$$L\xrightarrow{\sim}Ra_*a^*L.$$
Here $a^*L$ has components $a_n^*L$. This assertion holds for every such base change $Y\to X$, with the same ordinary adjunction-unit normalization.

source.place: Tag 0DHL, lemma-cohomological-descent-for-ph-hypercovering, and section-proper-hypercovering-spaces (schemes explicitly allowed); constant torsion module version by forgetting coefficients. Matching-map and termwise-proper conventions in that section.

proof.text: Prove by induction that $a_n$ is proper. The case $n=0$ is the matching-map assumption. Suppose $U_j\to X$ is proper for $j<n$. Express the finite matching limit $M_n$ as the equalizer of the two compatibility maps from the finite product $P$ of the objects in its face diagram to the finite product $Q$ of their targets. Products over $X$ are proper by iterating proper base change and composition (the empty product is $X$). The diagonal $Q\to Q\times_XQ$ is closed because $Q\to X$ is separated, by the definition of properness. Thus $M_n\to P$ is a closed immersion, being its pullback along the pair of compatibility maps. Closed immersions into proper schemes are proper. Hence $M_n\to X$ is proper, and composing with the assumed proper $U_n\to M_n$ proves the induction step. This equalizer description follows directly from the fibre-product universal property: a map to $P$ factors through it exactly when its components obey every face compatibility.

source.place: section-proper-hypercovering-spaces, termwise properness from the finite matching diagrams; geometric facts Tags 01W3, 01W4, 01W5.

proof.text: For $Y\to X$, put $U'_j=U_j\times_XY$. The matching object for $U'_\bullet$ is $M'_n=M_n\times_XY$: maps over $Y$ from a test scheme $T$ to either side are exactly compatible families of maps $T\to U_j$ over $X$, with the given map $T\to Y$. This identifies both the representing schemes and their matching maps. The latter are the base changes of $U_n\to M_n$, so properness and surjectivity follow from the cited stability statements. For $n=0$ the same argument says $M'_0=Y$. This also shows the termwise augmentations over $Y$ are proper.

source.place: section-proper-hypercovering-spaces; matching limits by their universal property; properness 01W4 and surjectivity 01S1.

proof.text: Work first with an abelian $K\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{Et}})$ with torsion cohomology. On $(\mathrm{Sch}/X)_{ph}$ every matching singleton is covering by the defining generators of the ph topology. Thus the given augmented simplicial scheme is a hypercover in this site. Apply the general site hypercover descent theorem, with $\mathcal C=(\mathrm{Sch}/X)_{ph}$ and terminal object $X/X$, to the complex $E=h_X^{-1}K$. Its conclusion gives the actual unit $E\to Rb_*b^{-1}E$ as an isomorphism. Slicing at the terminal object changes nothing, and slicing at $U_n/X$ gives $(\mathrm{Sch}/U_n)_{ph}$, since objects, morphisms and covering sieves in the two descriptions are the same. Inverse image is exact, so $E$ is bounded below.

source.place: Tag 0DHL proof, application of Tag 0D8N; proper singleton covers are built into the ph topology (0DES).

proof.text: Use the simplicial comparison square to obtain $h$ with components $h_n=h_{U_n}$ and $a h\simeq h_X b$. Set $A=a^{-1}K$ on the total etale topos, so $A_n=a_n^{-1}K$. All these component complexes are bounded below with torsion cohomology: inverse image is exact and sends an equation $m s=0$ locally to the same equation. The total inverse image is exact as well. The square identifies $h^{-1}A$ with $b^{-1}h_X^{-1}K$.

source.place: Tag 0DHJ and the comparison square used at the beginning of the proof of Tag 0DHL.

proof.text: For each $n$, apply the ph/etale torsion comparison on the scheme $U_n$ to $A_n$. It gives that $\eta_{h_n,A_n}:A_n\to Rh_{n,*}h_n^{-1}A_n$ is an isomorphism. The total-site derived component formula identifies the restriction of $\eta_{h,A}$ with precisely this component unit. Restriction is exact, so each cohomology sheaf of the cone of $\eta_{h,A}$ restricts to zero in every degree $n$. A total sheaf is a family of its components; hence these cohomology sheaves are zero. Thus the actual unit $\eta_{h,A}:A\to Rh_*h^{-1}A$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0DHL proof, first equality: component comparison 0DE5 and derived component formula 0D97.

proof.text:
The categories of abelian sheaves here are Grothendieck, by the ring-sheaf theorem applied to the integer sheaf. Their inverse images are exact. Write $\eta_f$ for the ordinary derived unit. The composite-unit formula and the comparison square identify the following two maps to the same derived direct image:
$$Ra_*(\eta_{h,a^{-1}K})\circ\eta_{a,K}
=Rh_{X,*}(\eta_{b,h_X^{-1}K})\circ\eta_{h_X,K}.$$
The first factor on the left is an isomorphism by step 5. The first factor on the right is an isomorphism by step 3, and its second factor is an isomorphism by the ph/etale comparison on $X$. Therefore $\eta_{a,K}$ is an isomorphism. This proves the abelian assertion with its unit normalization: the conclusion follows for the specified morphism, not merely from an abstract isomorphism between its source and target.

source.place: Tag 0DHL displayed chain of four equalities; composite-unit normalization in sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0D6E.

proof.text: For the constant ring $\Lambda$, use the generic inverse-image theorem to identify the exact module pullback with abelian inverse image after forgetting scalars. Apply the ringed coefficient-restriction counit theorem with $A=\mathbf Z$ and $R_X,R_Y$ the constant $\Lambda$ sheaves on the source and target of the augmentation. It gives $\kappa:V_YRf_{*,\Lambda}\simeq Rf_{*,\mathbf Z}V_X$ and $\tau:f^{-1}V_Y\simeq V_Xf^*_{\Lambda}$, with the stated counit equation. Here $f=a$, $X$ denotes the total topos, and $Y$ the base topos. To check the unit rather than merely the objects, transpose $\kappa_{f^*L}\circ V_Y\eta_{\Lambda,L}$ under the abelian derived adjunction. The counit equation changes this transpose to $V_X\varepsilon_{\Lambda,f^*L}\circ\tau_{Rf_*f^*L}\circ f^{-1}V_Y\eta_{\Lambda,L}$. Naturality of $\tau$ changes it to $V_X(\varepsilon_{\Lambda,f^*L}\circ f^*\eta_{\Lambda,L})\circ\tau_L=\tau_L$, by the triangle identity. This is also the transpose of $Rf_{*,\mathbf Z}(\tau_L)\circ\eta_{\mathbf Z,V_YL}$. Thus the forgotten module unit is exactly the abelian unit under these comparisons.

source.place: Canonical ringed coefficient restriction via 0D6J and the adjunctions; the unit identity is the transpose of the cited counit identity.

proof.text: Put $K=V_XL$ on the base scheme (now subscripts denote schemes again). Scalar forgetting is exact by the module-sheaf theorem, so $H^q(K)=V_XH^q(L)$. It is conservative on derived objects: if the forgotten cone has zero cohomology, the original cohomology module sheaves have zero underlying abelian sheaves and hence are zero. Since $m\Lambda=0$, every term and cohomology sheaf of $K$ is killed by $m$. Step 6 applies. Step 7 identifies its unit with the forgotten module unit, so conservativity proves that the module unit $L\to Ra_*a^*L$ is an isomorphism. The generic site-level results in step 7 apply to the total topos as well; no preservation of injectives by scalar forgetting is asserted.

source.place: 0D6J coefficient comparison, with exact/conservative forgetting and torsion checked directly.

proof.text: Finally let $Y\to X$ be arbitrary and let $L_Y$ be any bounded-below constant-$\Lambda$ complex on $Y_{\mathrm{Et}}$. Step 2 supplies all matching hypotheses for $U_\bullet\times_XY\to Y$. Repeat steps 3--8 with this scheme, this augmented diagram and $L_Y$. They give the ordinary unit $L_Y\to Ra_{Y,*}a_Y^*L_Y$ as an isomorphism. No claim that $L_Y$ is pulled back from $X$ was used; this proves the asserted universal statement for every complex on every base change.

source.place: Tag 0DHL applied after arbitrary base change, using step 2.

tool_uses.why: Generic geometric stability needed to express a finite matching limit as a closed subscheme of a proper product; no node of this unit supplies it.
Generic surjectivity stability needed for universal matching maps; no node of this unit supplies it.

Applied to the integer sheaf on the total and base sites, this supplies the Grothendieck hypotheses for the generic derived-adjunction normalization.
